correctness.rationale: For t>1 the largest eigenvalue is at least 1, so det(G_n−t^(−2)I)<0 is equivalent to the claimed small-eigenvalue event. The Schur complement yields Q<n t^(−2)[σ²+(Z−μ)²/(1−t^(−2))]. Its radius lies between R(Z)/t and (1+O(t^(−2)))R(Z)/t uniformly, so a squeeze preserves the sharp equivalent including a possible log. The Euclidean diagonal-coordinate Jacobian is √n; on compact mean intervals the rescaled cross section has volume V_(n−1) R(z)^(n−1). Near zero the intermediate region z≥C/t has product density uniformly within 1+O(1/C) of f(z)^n; the layer z<C/t is O_C(t^(−nα)), and the reflected estimates use β. Thus at n(α−1)=−1 the log coefficient is unchanged by the fixed lower cutoff C/t. In each subcritical corner the rescaling x_i=y_i/t gives J_n, with integrable product powers on bounded boxes and envelope proportional to s^(n(a−1)) at diagonal coordinate s≫1. This justifies both convergence and strict positivity, gives the convergence threshold for J_n, and handles tied endpoint contributions by disjoint localization. Layer cake gives divergence also at the moment boundary. As independent checks, for two uniform samples the exact event integrates in mean/difference coordinates with Jacobian 1; t times the probability has limit 4∫_0^1 sqrt(1/12+(z−1/2)^2) dz=2/√3+asinh(√3)/3. For n=3 the corresponding integral without the square root equals 1/6 and gives π√3/2. These analytic formulas are replayable from the displayed integrals; no supplied script was executed and no simulated tail was needed to justify the theorem.

evidence: Partition the support into a finite collection of interior intervals and two endpoint intervals of length d. Because Q=O(t^(−2)), samples crossing a fixed interior cut must all be within O(1/t) of that cut; they contribute O(t^(−n)). In an interior interval I, squeeze R and f by their extrema. Royen's exact uniform result, scaled to I, gives leading coefficient brackets √n V_(n−1)|I| (inf or sup f)^n (inf or sup R)^(n−1). Mesh refinement produces the exact weighted Riemann integral.

In [0,d], squeeze the Beta density by (1+O(d))x^(a−1)/B and R by its endpoint extrema. The pure-power total multiplier is (d^a/(aB))^n, and the argument of Royen's F_Q is (R/(dt))². If na<n−1 or na=n−1 the d powers cancel, and log(1/x) gives 2 log t. In the critical case Royen's (50) gives C_an=(√n V_(n−1) a^n)/2, so the frozen coefficient follows exactly. A bulk-order endpoint with 0<a<1 has coefficient O(d^(na−n+1)); for a≥1 the uniform comparison with bounded density suffices. Repeat after reflection, adding tied leading endpoints.

For the subcritical constant, the integral of (h^-_a)^n+(h^+_a)^n in Royen (50) equals a^n √(π/n)∫_{y_i>0} exp(−Q(y))∏y_i^(a−1)dy, by integrating over the common center on the real line. Homogeneity gives the last integral Γ(1+na/2) J_n(a,1), so the (50) coefficient is a^n J_n(a,1). The interval scaling therefore gives exactly J_n(a,R(e))/B^n, not merely its exponent.

originality.rationale: The exact all-n constants and three regimes are recoverable from existing sharp constant-radius small-ball results, not just from bounds on the exponent. Royen's uniform thin-cylinder asymptotic and exact pure-power Theorem 3 can be localized by simple density and radius sandwiches after the affine 2×2 Gram identity. This produces the exact mean-weighted constants for all positive Beta shapes; the older three-sample Beta result independently exhibits the same mechanism in the n=3 slice. The norm-specific statement is not quoted verbatim in those sources, but the claimed exact information is mechanically implied as detailed below.
